subject: Myrtle Street 40B Development Alternative Site Plan
overview: The board reviewed an alternative conceptual site plan for a proposed 40B housing development that shifts building massing and reconfigures site access to address neighborhood concerns. No final vote was taken, but the applicant was directed to refine the plan's streetscape and parking details for the next session.

items.title: Architectural Peer Review and Alternative Concept Plan
items.summary: Cliff Bomer presented a summary of architectural peer review sessions focusing on site integration, followed by the applicant’s introduction of a revised concept that shifts the building footprint east and increases pervious open space.

items.title: Landscape Design and Site Circulation
items.summary: The design team detailed conceptual landscape buffers, a new delivery loop on Myrtle Street, and a shift in garage access to the Fellsway side to mitigate neighborhood traffic.

items.title: Board and City Staff Discussion
items.summary: Board members and city planners questioned the necessity of the proposed parking ratios, the visual impact of surface parking along Amaranth Avenue, and the isolation created by elevated residential courtyards.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents raised concerns regarding the narrowness of Myrtle Street for increased delivery traffic, shadow impacts on neighboring homes, and the existing capacity limits of local MBTA bus routes.

items.title: Next Steps and Scheduling
items.summary: The board continued the hearing to February 15, directing the applicant to return with a refined site plan that addresses feedback on building positioning and parking before proceeding to civil engineering and traffic reviews.
